FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Third Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Textile Machinery and Accessories Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textiles Division Council. 


This standard has been formulated to provide guidance to the manufacturers of cotton cambs for use in jute looms. 
This standard would ensure the manufacture of cotton cambs of acceptable quality. 


This standard was originally published in 1961 and subsequently revised in 1974 and 1990. This standard was 
revised in This revision has been made in the light of experience gained since its publication and to incorporate 
the following major changes: 


a) Title of the standard has been modified; 
b) Marking, packing and sampling clauses have been modified; and 
c) References to Indian Standards have been updated. 


The composition of the committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is listed in Annex C. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 2022 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (second revision)’. The number of significant places retained 
in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 1938 : 2023 


Indian Standard 


TEXTILES — COTTON CAMBS FOR USE IN JUTE LOOMS — 
SPECIFICATION 


( Third Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard specifies requirements for cotton 
cambs for use in jute looms. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards listed in Annex A contain provisions 
which, through reference in this text, constitute 
provisions of this standard. At the time of 
publication, the editions indicated were valid. All 
standards are subject to revision, and parties to 
agreements based on this standard are encouraged to 
investigate the possibility of applying the most 
recent editions of the standards listed in 
Annex A. 


3 MANUFACTURE AND WORKMANSHIP 


In a camb, the healds shall be bound as shown in 
Fig. 1. АП the mail eyes in a camb shall be of same 
type (dimensions) and so threaded that all are set at 
the same angle. The eyes shall be at the centre of 
healds unless otherwise specified by the purchaser. 
The cambs shall be varnished all along the depth 
except for small portions of camb near the top and 
bottom foundation bands. The depth of the 
unvarnished portion of each side of cambs shall not 
exceed 25 mm. The varnished surface should be 
smooth, glossy and pliable and free from lumps, 
cracks and stickiness. 


4 REQUIREMENTS 
4.1 Mail Eye 


Mail eyes shall conform to the requirements of 


Table 1 unless otherwise specified in the contract or 
order. 


4.2 Distance from top to the centre of the mail eye, 
Fı (see Fig. 1) shall be same as distance from the 
centre to the bottom of the mail eye, Fo. 


4.3 Twine 


4.3.1 Unless otherwise specified in the contract or 
order, the count of yarn used and number of folds 
applied in the twine used for the top and bottom 
leashes (see Fig. 1) of the camb shall be as follows: 


Porter of Count of Yarn No. of 
Camb Folds 
4 to 8 29.5 tex (20° cotton) 32 
Above 8 29.5 tex (20* cotton) 28 
4.4 Depth of Camb 


4.4.1 Unless otherwise specified in the contract or 
order, the depth of camb (inclusive of depth of 


foundation bands) shall be 355 5 mm when tested 
according to the method given in Annex B. 
NOTE — For obtaining effective depth of camb, the 


observed values should be corrected for thickness of the top 
and bottom foundation bands. 


4.5 Width of Camb 


4.5.1 The distance between the two extreme healds 
in a set (overall width) shall be as declared by the 
manufacturer or as marked on it.

6 PACKING 


Each camb, while it is on the stave during the 
process of varnishing, shall be ‘folded’ and ‘leashed’ 
by the tail ends of the top and bottom foundation 
bands, so as to separate the odd and even eyes. A 
suitable number of these cambs tied together 
(forming a bundle) shall be wrapped in waterproof 
paper (see IS 3962). 


7 SAMPLING 


To ascertain the conformity of cotton cambs for use 
in jute looms, to the requirements of this 
specification, single sampling plan with Inspection 
Level I and Acceptance Quality Level (AQL) of 
2.5 percent given in Tables 1 and 2-A of IS 2500 
(Part 1) shall be followed unless otherwise agreed to 
between the buyer and the seller. 


IS 1938 : 2023

ANNEX B 
(Clause 4.4.1) 


METHOD FOR DETERMINATION OF DEPTH OF CAMB 


ВЈ ATMOSPHERIC CONDITIONS FOR 
TESTING 


B-1.1 The test shall be carried out in the prevailing 
atmospheric conditions with relative humidity 
between 40 percent to 90 percent. 


B-2 TEST PROCEDURE 


B-2.1 Take a stand provided with two hooks (at a 
distance of 70 cm to 75 cm from each other) to 
support the top stave of the camb, the depth of which 
is to be measured. Hang two pans at the bottom stave 
exactly below the two hooks on the top stave. The 
depth of camb is measured from outside edge of the 


top foundation band to the outside edge of the 
bottom foundation band by applying the following 
load: 


Resultant Tex (Cotton Count) Load on Each 


of Camb Twine Pan 
Up to 150 (above 4°) 0 
151 to 200 (3° to 4°) 30 
201 to 300 (2° to 3°) 40 
301 to 600 (1° to 2°) 50 
Above 600 (below 1°) 60

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Head (Publication & Sales), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: TXD 14 (20062).
